slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 14, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,620.25, down 36.73 points (−0.5%) after trading between 7,592.28 and 7,647.99.
The Nasdaq Composite lost 0.6% to 26,186.41; the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.3% to 52,421.20; and the Russell 2000 was off 0.4% at 2,892.24.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 8.0% to 17.10 from a prior close of 15.84, with an intraday high of 18.17 — a higher fear gauge on a red day for the large-cap benchmarks.

Semiconductor and equipment names carried much of the megacap weakness: ASML closed −7.3% at 1,575.15, Broadcom −4.8% at 344.72, AMD −4.4% at 493.41, NVIDIA −3.4% at 210.96, and Taiwan Semiconductor −3.5% at 418.01.
Intel, among the most active symbols in the session list, was −5.6% at 97.19.

Communication Services was the strongest Nasdaq sector in the data (+1.6% average), with Netflix +3.8% to 80.32, Alphabet +3.2% to 349.39, and Meta +2.7% to 665.60.
Technology still averaged +0.6% despite the chip selloff, illustrating a split inside the growth complex.

Financial Services averaged +0.7% on Nasdaq, but Bank of America bucked that tone at −5.1% and 59.47 on volume above 61 million shares.
Defensive consumer names showed modest gains: Walmart +1.8% to 109.08, Costco +1.6% to 918.91, Procter & Gamble +0.6% to 146.13, and UnitedHealth +1.2% to 383.55.

Utilities (−3.1%) and Real Estate (−2.6%) were the weakest sector averages in the screen; Energy averaged −1.0% even as Brent crude futures rose 1.3% to 107.01 and the United States Oil Fund (USO) gained 1.1% to 156.66.
Basic Materials averaged −0.7%.

Gold futures (GC) were essentially flat, +0.1% to 4,354.40.
The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP) ticked up 0.4% to 28.17; EUR/USD was −0.2% at 1.15.
Bitcoin USD closed −0.5% at 77,809.57.

Treasury yields in the Sept. 11 curve snapshot showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.33 percentage points — context for headlines noting the 10-year briefly above 5% before settling near 5.0%.
The U.S. calendar logged low-impact bill auctions: the 3-month at 4.0% and the 6-month at 4.1%.

Overseas indexes in the bundle were mixed versus the U.S. close: Nikkei 225 +0.9% at 64,082.36, FTSE 100 +0.4% at 10,697.57, Hang Seng −0.4% at 24,823.79, and the Germany proxy (EWG) −0.4% at 42.71.
No earnings actuals were listed in the injected earnings calendar for this session.

slots.body:
Monday 12:30 p.m.

Consensus: 14.75.
